item.content:encoded:
Premier League stars shine among 2026 Ballon d’Or nominees Manchester City striker Erling Haaland reached 100 Premier League goals in December 2025, achieving the milestone in just 111 appearances. He scored 38 goals in 52 appearances for City across all competitions during the 2025/26 season. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 19:30 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 19:30 IST

Bruno Fernandes. (Photo: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Premier League players have made their mark among the nominees for the 2026 Ballon d’Or, with Opta statistics highlighting standout performances across the 2025/26 season. Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes recorded 22 assists in the Premier League during the 2025/26 campaign, setting a new competition record. He also created 142 chances in the league, the most of any player across Europe’s big-five leagues, according to Opta 2025/26 season. Manchester City striker Erling Haaland reached 100 Premier League goals in December 2025, achieving the milestone in just 111 appearances. He scored 38 goals in 52 appearances for City across all competitions during the 2025/26 season. Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhães kept 17 clean sheets in the Premier League during the campaign, more than any other defender in the competition. He recorded 24 clean sheets across all competitions for the Gunners. His Arsenal teammate William Saliba completed 67 passes per 90 minutes in the Premier League, the highest rate among Arsenal players during the season. Arsenal also won 71% of the matches in which he featured, compared with 57% of games without him. Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice contributed five goals and nine assists across all competitions in the 2025/26 season. He created 96 chances, the most by any English player across Europe’s big-five leagues in all competitions. The nominees also include Rodri, whose 2025/26 season statistics reflect his time at Manchester City, and Marc Cucurella, whose campaign included performances for Chelsea. Their inclusion highlights the contributions of players with Premier League connections among this year’s nominees. The statistics showcase the range of performances recognised among the nominees, from Fernandes’ record-breaking creativity and Haaland’s goalscoring milestones to the defensive consistency of Arsenal’s back line and Rice’s influence in midfield. (ANI)

item.title: Google, Glance partner to bring AI-powered shopping to Android TVs in India, US, Japan
item.description: Google and Glance have partnered to bring artificial intelligence (AI)-powered shopping and product discovery to Android TVs in India, the United States and Japan, aiming to turn television screens ...
item.content:encoded:
Google, Glance partner to bring AI-powered shopping to Android TVs in India, US, Japan Google and Glance have partnered to bring artificial intelligence (AI)-powered shopping and product discovery to Android TVs in India, the United States and Japan, aiming to turn television screens into interactive platforms for lifestyle inspiration and online shopping. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 19:16 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 19:16 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Google and Glance have partnered to bring artificial intelligence (AI)-powered shopping and product discovery to Android TVs in India, the United States and Japan, aiming to turn television screens into interactive platforms for lifestyle inspiration and online shopping. The partnership will allow users to explore products across categories such as fashion, home décor, travel, food and wellness through an interactive experience on supported Android TV devices. The integration aims to transform the television screen when it is not being actively used into a platform for product discovery. The experience will be opt-in, allowing users to choose between the default Google Backdrop and the Glance-powered ambient screen. Naveen Tewari, CEO and Founder of InMobi and Glance, said the partnership would help move television screens beyond their traditional use. “We are moving beyond the era of the ‘dormant’ screen,” Tewari said. “By combining the scale of Google’s Android TV ecosystem with Glance’s AI-first commerce models, we are turning the living room into a space where inspiration meets intent. Whether it’s fashion, home décor, or travel, we’re making shopping and discovery seamless, immersive, and interactive,” he added. The new experience will include an AI-powered shopping agent that connects product discovery across mobile phones and televisions. Powered by hundreds of retailer integrations, the system will help users explore curated products and move from discovering items to purchasing them through integrated retail partners. Users will also be able to explore high-definition content across different lifestyle categories. The platform will use its AI technology to offer contextual lifestyle simulations and try-on visualisations. Another feature, called “Shop the Look”, will allow users to interact with curated looks displayed on their television screens and purchase products through integrated retail partners. The partnership is expected to expand Glance's distribution through Google's Android TV ecosystem. According to the announcement, Glance already has partnerships with Airtel and DIRECTV, and the latest collaboration will extend its reach to supported Android TV devices in the United States, India and Japan. For Google, the integration aims to increase the utility of the Android TV platform by developing it into an interactive lifestyle hub. For Glance, it provides an opportunity to bring its AI-powered commerce experience to more households. Glance is now available on supported Android TV devices in the three markets, according to the announcement. (ANI)

item.title: Chinese AI powers half of Korea's new models: study
item.description: Nearly half of the artificial intelligence (AI) models released by South Korean developers this year were built on Chinese technology, predominantly Alibaba's Qwen, according to a study cited by The ...
item.content:encoded:
Chinese AI powers half of Korea's new models: study Nearly half of the artificial intelligence (AI) models released by South Korean developers this year were built on Chinese technology, predominantly Alibaba's Qwen, according to a study cited by The Korea Herald, raising questions about the country's efforts to develop its own AI models. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 19:08 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 19:08 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

South Korea

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Nearly half of the artificial intelligence (AI) models released by South Korean developers this year were built on Chinese technology, predominantly Alibaba's Qwen, according to a study cited by The Korea Herald, raising questions about the country's efforts to develop its own AI models. The report, released Friday by private think tank Rockbridge Network Korea and authored by Hanyang University business professor Choi Seong-jin, examined how Chinese AI is being used in Korea through developer activity, app usage and corporate surveys. Of the 1,845 AI model derivatives published by Korea-linked accounts on global model-sharing platform Hugging Face between January and August, 49.3 per cent were based on Chinese foundation models. US models accounted for 35.9 per cent, while Korean models clocked 14.9 per cent, The Korea Herald reported. The Chinese share has rapidly climbed from just 1.2 per cent in 2023 and 22 per cent last year. Over the same period, the US share fell from 79.5 per cent. Qwen alone accounted for 864 derivatives, or 46.8 per cent of this year's total, far ahead of Google's Gemma at 14.7 per cent and Meta's Llama at 13.8 per cent. Among Korean-developed models, LG AI Research's Exaone ranked fourth with 171 derivatives, or 9.3 per cent of the total, followed by Kakao's Kanana in sixth place with 49, or 2.7 per cent. Together, Korean foundation models accounted for just 14.9 per cent of new releases, less than one-third of Alibaba's Qwen alone. The findings raise questions about South Korea's government-backed sovereign AI program, which has received some 200 billion won (USD 151 million) in support to develop homegrown alternatives to foreign models. LG AI Research, SK Telecom and startup Upstage advanced to the next stage in August, after Naver Cloud was eliminated earlier this year for using components from Alibaba's Qwen model, failing to meet the program's technology independence requirements. Chinese models are already heavily used in some Korean AI services, particularly where operating costs matter. "We mainly use Chinese models such as Qwen and DeepSeek for services with high user traffic," said an official at a Korean AI startup. Qwen's appeal also extends beyond price. The report cited its wide range of model sizes, support for 119 languages and readily available development tools that make it easier to customize. Chinese AI's popularity among Korean developers is largely absent from conventional usage figures. No Chinese chatbot ranked among Korea's 10 most-used AI apps in July, and researchers found no references to Chinese models in roughly 1,900 public GitHub repositories belonging to 36 major Korean companies. The report said these figures offer an incomplete picture because developers can download Chinese models and use them without relying on Chinese companies' online services. "Simply blocking access to Chinese AI services does not mean Chinese AI is no longer being used," it said. Security does remain a concern. In a survey of 102 small and midsized businesses, 80.2 per cent cited fears of data leaks, compared with 31.3 per cent concerned about model performance and quality. The report also warned that relying too heavily on a single model could leave developers vulnerable if its provider changes licensing terms or stops releasing new versions. "For Korean open models to gain traction among developers, performance alone is not enough," Choi wrote. "They also need commercially viable licenses, a range of model sizes and the tools developers need to customize them." (ANI)

item.title: Trump terms "no swap" release of US citizen Stephen Hubbard from Russia "unprecedented"
item.description: The prisoner release was initially disclosed by Russian President Vladimir Putin during a meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff, according to Russian news agencies.
item.content:encoded:
Trump terms "no swap" release of US citizen Stephen Hubbard from Russia "unprecedented" The prisoner release was initially disclosed by Russian President Vladimir Putin during a meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff, according to Russian news agencies. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 19:06 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 19:06 IST

US citizen Stephen Hubbard, accused of serving as a mercenary for Ukraine against Russia in the course of a military conflict, appears in a court hearing, in Moscow, Russia. (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump stated on Wednesday that Stephen Hubbard, an American citizen previously taken captive by Russian forces inside Ukraine, has secured his freedom and is currently returning to the United States. The prisoner release was initially disclosed by Russian President Vladimir Putin during a meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff, according to Russian news agencies. Putin reportedly indicated that Hubbard was at Pulkovo Airport in Saint Petersburg, adding that Witkoff expressed gratitude towards the Russian leader for the liberation. Hubbard, a retired English educator in his seventies, received a nearly seven-year custodial sentence during a closed trial conducted in October 2024 concerning allegations of undertaking “mercenary work” supporting Ukraine, an accusation he contests. Trump emphasised that Hubbard's freedom was secured independently of any prisoner exchange framework with Moscow. “Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family,” the American leader conveyed via his Truth Social account. “The United States, out of respect for President Trump, was not required to give anything in return — an unprecedented situation for Russia. There was no ‘swap’ necessary for this release.” Trump additionally connected Hubbard's liberation to the recent pause implemented regarding specific American trade tariffs and sanctions directed at Moscow. “If sanctions would have been placed, certainly those negotiations would have come to a complete and total halt,” he further stated on the platform. Wednesday's announcement transpired as Witkoff met with Putin to brief the Russian leader on his discussions with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Oslo the previous day, which the American envoy characterised as constructive. Trump mentioned on Tuesday that he had personally appealed to Putin for Hubbard's freedom. “I’ve been talking to him at length. I’ve asked him to release him. Let’s see what happens,” Trump informed reporters in Washington. Following the development, Witkoff conveyed that Trump and the entire nation extended their appreciation for Stephen Hubbard's release, describing Putin as a humanitarian. (ANI)
